messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood follow-up — procurement readiness & commercial path

Hi Liam / Priya,

Thanks again for the conversation today — really helpful to understand Acme's inference requirements and procurement rules. Quick recap and proposed next steps to keep procurement moving: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary use case: customer-facing generative features in Production by Q3; estimated 10M tokens/month initially, spike patterns during marketing campaigns.
- Security/regulatory: must support VPC/private deployment later this year; initially ok with hosted if data controls and contractual protections in place.
- Procurement preference: procurement typically requires a PO for any vendor > $50k / year; card is only for low-dollar pilots.
- Marketplace: your platform team asked about deploying via cloud marketplace (GCP/AWS) to simplify purchase order and invoicing.

Open commercial & procurement questions
1) Do you need an SOW or will a subscription order (PO + subscription term) suffice for initial commitment?
2) Are you planning to buy via marketplace (AWS/GCP) or direct Redwood contract? That changes billing flow and timing.
3) For deployment mode, would you prefer hosted (fast onboarding) or Dedicated/Private (predictable throughput + data isolation)? Procurement might require Dedicated/Private for full production.

Attachments I’m including here: pricing sheet (high level), hosted vs dedicated one-pager, and a starter SOW template we can tailor.

Proposed next steps
- You: confirm whether procurement will accept a subscription PO (we can provide PO-ready quote) or if a full SOW + MSA is required.
- We: put together two commercial paths (1) hosted, month-to-month + optional marketplace invoice; (2) Dedicated with 12-month commit + billing via PO + SOW. Will include estimated unit economics and transition plan to private/VPC.
- If useful, we can loop in our legal/P&S for an accelerated procurement packet.

Would love confirmation on the PO vs card question and whether marketplace is preferred. Happy to jump on a quick call with procurement if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — great recap. A few clarifications from procurement side: 

- PO vs card: For anything expected to exceed ~ $20k annually we need to go PO route. Pilots under $5k can go on card. So likely PO for our initial expected spend.
- Marketplace: We prefer marketplace purchases where possible — it speeds up invoicing and avoids lengthy vendor onboarding. That said, if Dedicated requires direct contracting we can evaluate the tradeoffs.
- SOW: procurement will accept a PO for a subscription if we have a clear statement of work/attachment that outlines deliverables and support SLAs.

I can connect you with our Procurement Ops lead if needed — looping Tom here. Also looping Priya for technical/infra confirmation.

Liam
Liam O'Connor

- Deployment: Our infra team prefers Dedicated for production for performance predictability; hosted is acceptable for a short pilot but procurement will push for Dedicated once we exceed pilot thresholds.
- Security: we need to confirm data residency and log retention controls (SOC2 + audit log exports). Legal will likely require those in the MSA.

Thanks — noted and appreciate the clarity. Per your ask, attached is a concise commercial paths doc that maps to Acme's purchasing rules. Below is a short summary of the three options and recommended path based on procurement preferences.

Commercial paths (summary)
A) Hosted pilot (fastest onboarding)
- Purpose: 4–6 week validation / PoC, low friction sign-up.
- Billing: card or small PO (we can issue a PO-ready quote for $5k–$15k).
- Pros: fastest time-to-value, no infra setup.
- Cons: not suitable for long-term production if procurement requires data isolation.

B) Dedicated (recommended for Production)
- Purpose: Dedicated GPU pool, predictable throughput, KV cache and performance SLAs.
- Billing: 12-month commit with PO. We can support quarterly invoicing against the PO.
- Pros: meets procurement's preference for PO + SOW, better performance and isolation.
- Cons: requires lead time for capacity reservation; we’ll include an onboarding migration plan.

C) Private / VPC (for regulated workloads)
- Purpose: Customer-managed VPC or on-prem deployment for full control.
- Billing: Enterprise licensing + support fees, typically direct contract + SOW + MSA.
- Pros: maximum isolation/compliance.
- Cons: longer procurement and setup timeline.

Pricing & commits
- We included two pricing profiles in the attached sheet: On-demand (hosted) unit pricing; 12-month committed pricing (Dedicated) with staged commit discounts. Example: for 10M tokens/month, Dedicated 12-month commit reduces unit cost by ~35% vs hosted on-demand.

Marketplace option
- We can offer a marketplace listing (AWS/GCP) for the hosted product which supports marketplace procurement flow. For Dedicated, marketplace is possible but often procurement prefers direct PO so we’ll provide both flows in the quote.

Next steps
1) I’ll prepare a PO-ready quote for the Dedicated 12-month path and a marketplace quote for hosted pilot.
2) If procurement wants, we can schedule a short call (15–20m) with our billing/legal ops to align on PO wording and invoicing cadence.
3) Dev and Aditya are standing by to provide technical attachments (SOC2 summary, network diagrams) if Legal requests them.

If that all sounds good I’ll push the two quotes today and share HubSpot links and DocuSign URL for signature.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
